name: VERIFY: The Meridian Fact Channel
creator: Axiom Consortium (multi-corponation joint venture)
description: Launched in 2210 as a joint initiative by six major corponations in response to the credibility crisis triggered by the Okafor-Steinberg revelations, VERIFY presents itself as an independent fact-checking and media transparency broadcast available across all neural feed tiers. Its production values are deliberately austere — plain interfaces, citation overlays, correction logs — designed to signal rigor. Critics immediately noted that VERIFY's ownership consortium includes every major media entity it claims to independently evaluate, and that its 'corrections' consistently exonerate corponation-affiliated sources while flagging underground and pirate broadcasts.
medium: neural feed (all tiers), legacy video, public holographic display
cultural_impact: VERIFY succeeded in its primary goal — providing Tier 2-3 audiences with a corporate-branded alternative to independent journalism that feels credible — and has measurably reduced engagement with gray-market investigative feeds among that demographic.
controversy: VERIFY has never issued a correction to any content produced by its six founding corponation owners. It has issued 847 corrections to underground and pirate sources in its first four years. The ratio is treated as self-evident by its critics and as irrelevant by its defenders.
story_hooks: A VERIFY researcher — genuinely believing in the network's stated mission — discovers internal data showing systematic suppression of corrections to corponation sources; they need help deciding what to do with it and who to trust.

VERIFY is about to issue a 'correction' that will discredit a the Gray Zone Frequency emergency report — the report is accurate, and someone on the inside is trying to get the truth out before the correction airs.

VERIFY's editorial algorithm has been quietly updated; a pattern analyst notices it now pre-emptively flags certain types of stories before they're even published — suggesting it's receiving advance intelligence about what independent journalists are working on.
